title: Access & Crypto Requirements PRD for Private Deployments
creator: Sophie Nguyen
description: PRD capturing concrete requirements, acceptance criteria, and a role-based sign-off checklist for SSO (SAML & OIDC), RBAC, audit logging, and key management (KMS/HSM) for Private (VPC/on-prem) Redwood deployments. This document scopes what is in MVP v1 for enterprise customers and records decisions and unresolved questions for follow-up.
scope_summary: MVP: SAML + OIDC SSO integrations with SCIM user provisioning optional in v1
RBAC: project-level roles + service account model; audit-only deny/allow policy enforcement in v1
Audit logs: immutable, tamper-evident event stream with export to customer SIEM
KMS/HSM: support for customer-managed keys via cloud KMS and PKCS#11 HSMs; BYOK workflow documented
Excluded from v1: fine-grained attribute-based access control, deep entitlement analytics
scope_changes: 2025-03-03: Narrowed KMS support to cloud KMS + PKCS#11 HSM adapters instead of full HSM fleet management (decision to defer HSM provisioning UI to v2).
2025-03-04: Deferred SCIM user provisioning from v1 to v1.1 due to integration complexity identified in engineering spike.
2025-03-05: Added explicit audit export to S3 and syslog endpoints after customer request during discovery calls.
acceptance_criteria: SSO: Tenant can configure SAML IdP metadata or OIDC provider and perform end-to-end login with test user within private deployment (documented test steps).
RBAC: Admin can create roles and assign them to users and service accounts; enforcement prevents non-admin access to model deployment endpoints; unit and e2e tests exist.
Audit logs: All authentication, authorization, and key-management events are logged; logs are append-only; customers can export logs to S3 with retention controls; retention default is 90 days.
KMS: Customers can register a cloud KMS key (AWS/GCP/Azure) or provide PKCS#11 HSM credentials; encryption of at-rest secrets in the control plane uses the registered key.
Documentation: Admin guide, runbook for key rotation, and an incident playbook for key compromise are published in Confluence and linked from the console.
Automation: IaC example (Terraform) for wiring KMS + SSO config is provided and validated in a test environment.
signoff_checklist: Security PM: verifies acceptance criteria completeness and risk register entry
Security Engineering: approves threat model and mitigations, signs off on KMS/HSM design
Infrastructure/Private Deploy Eng: validates deployability in VPC and HSM connectivity
SRE/Reliability: confirms audit log durability and observability SLOs
Legal/Compliance: confirms audit export and data residency meet contractual clauses
Customer Success: validates runbooks and admin documentation for first customer onboarding
implementation_notes: Use existing identity connector infra (ENG-1984) for SAML/OIDC handshake; extend metadata validator to accept self-signed certs for on-prem IdPs.
Introduce a service-account concept scoped to project IDs and limit token TTL to 24 hours for v1; long-lived keys migrate to KMS-wrapped secrets.
Audit store will be write-once S3 bucket with object locks when available; supplement with syslog forwarder for SIEM integration.
risk_register: Key compromise risk: mitigations include mandatory KMS usage for control plane secrets and documented emergency rotation playbook.
Integration variance: on-prem IdPs may require manual troubleshooting; include troubleshooting checklist and success criteria for onboarding.
Data residency: customers in EU may require local log storage; solution includes configurable log export endpoints per-region.
